exposure: Participation in a hemorrhage quality-improvement collaborative
cohort: Women with a diagnosis of obstetric hemorrhage during delivery hospitalization in California between 2011 and 2016 (n=73,476)
finding: A large-scale quality improvement collaborative reduced rates of severe maternal morbidity due to hemorrhage in all races and reduced the performance gap between Black and White women.
mod_finding: A quality improvement collaborative focused on hemorrhage management was found to reduce severe maternal morbidity rates due to hemorrhage across all racial groups, with a greater benefit observed among Black women, narrowing the performance gap between Black and white women.
